rule: Only the user's explicit accept or decline decision changes a review group status.

lesson10-admonitive-meaning.acceptedJob: Treat the admonitive as a positive cautionary warning or advice, never as an inherently negative prohibition.

lesson10-admonitive-vnc-formation.acceptedJob: Build only nonpast admonitive VNCs from the perfective stem with the correct class-conditioned tense morph and number dyad.

lesson10-affirmative-admonition-system.acceptedJob: Build affirmative admonition sentences with obligatory mā, optional nēn, participant-based warning role, and no false prohibition or wish reading.

lesson10-class-a-admonitions.acceptedJob: Build and interpret singular and plural Class A affirmative admonitions through the shared admonitive system.

lesson10-class-b-admonitions.acceptedJob: Build and interpret singular and plural Class B affirmative admonitions with zero tense and the correct number shapes.

lesson10-class-c-admonitions.acceptedJob: Build and interpret singular and plural Class C affirmative admonitions from the correct perfective stem.

lesson10-class-d-admonitions.acceptedJob: Build Class D admonitions and preserve appropriate warning or advice interpretation for human and nonhuman subjects.

lesson10-negative-admonitions.acceptedJob: Build negative admonitions with ah and obligatory mā nēn as a cancellation of warning, never as a prohibition or a Lesson 9 ca construction.

lesson10-general-vnc-contrasts.acceptedJob: Preserve second-person x or xi and plural morphology as dependable contrasts among admonitive, optative, present, and preterit forms.

lesson10-class-a-contrasts.acceptedJob: Generate the full Class A contrast paradigm and preserve every exact form, morphological distinction, and reading warning.

lesson10-class-b-contrasts.acceptedJob: Generate the full Class B contrast paradigm, preserve the mā huetz word boundary, and enforce mā and antecessive distinctions.

lesson10-class-c-contrasts.acceptedJob: Generate the full Class C contrast paradigm and enforce its stem, glottal-stop, mā, and antecessive distinctions.
